title: What Is a Source in an AI Answer?
description: A source is any page an AI engine pulls a fact from, whether it ends up as a citation or not. Here's what makes an engine trust one source over another.
focusKeyword: what is a source in AI search
bodyMarkdown:
Quick answer

A source, in AI search, is any page an engine reads and pulls information from while building an answer. Not every source becomes a visible citation (you can read about that distinction in our citation and mention posts), but every citation and most mentions start life as a source the AI decided to trust.

Key takeaways
  • "Source" is the broad term. Citation and mention are two different outcomes a source can lead to.
  • An AI engine usually reads several candidate sources before picking which ones to use in its answer.
  • Trust signals (clarity, structure, named authorship, freshness) decide which sources make the cut.
  • You can make your page a stronger candidate source without needing to guess at the algorithm.
If citation and mention are the two outcomes, source is the raw material. Before an AI engine can cite or mention anything, it first has to read a set of candidate pages and decide which of them actually deserve to shape the answer. Those candidate pages are sources. ## How does an AI engine pick which sources to actually trust? There isn't one universal rulebook (each engine, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, weighs things slightly differently), but a few signals come up consistently across how these systems are documented and how pages that get used tend to look: | Signal | Why it helps a page get treated as a trustworthy source | |---|---| | A direct, clearly stated answer | Easier for the model to extract and quote confidently | | Named, specific details (a figure, a date, a named study) | Easier to verify and attribute than a vague claim | | Structured data (schema markup) | Gives the model an explicit, machine-readable version of the fact, not just prose to interpret | | Freshness | A page that's clearly current is safer to rely on than one with no visible date | | Readable by the crawler at all | A page the crawler can't fetch or parse can't become a source, no matter how good the content is | [[chart:0]] ## Is a source the same thing as a backlink or a reference? Not quite. A backlink is a link someone else chose to place, built up over time, mainly used by classic search engines as a trust signal. A source, in this context, is simply a page the AI engine itself decided to read and rely on for a specific answer, decided fresh each time, with no link-building involved. A page with zero backlinks can absolutely become a trusted source if it answers the question clearly and the crawler can read it. > The AI isn't asking "how popular is this page." It's asking "does this specific page answer this specific question clearly enough for me to rely on it right now." ## Can my page be a source without ever becoming a visible citation? Yes, and this happens more than people realize. A page can genuinely influence an AI's answer, shaping the wording or the facts it includes, without that page ever being named directly. This is closer to the "mention" end of the spectrum: the AI absorbed something from the page but didn't formally credit it as the source of a specific claim. It's one reason citation counts alone don't tell the whole story of your AI visibility. ## How do I make my page a stronger candidate source? The practical version of all the signals above comes down to a few concrete things: state your key answer plainly near the top of the page, back claims with real, named data instead of vague generalizations, add structured data where it fits the content type, and keep the page visibly current. For the complete, checkable version of this, see the AEO & GEO checklist, which lays out every individual check in one place. ## How do I know if my page is even being read as a candidate source at all? Start with the free LLM Access Check, which shows you exactly what GPTBot, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot and others actually receive when they fetch your page. If the crawler can't read it, it can never become a source in the first place, regardless of how good the content is. Once you know the crawlers can read it, the Full AEO & GEO Audit scores the page against the trust signals above and ranks what to fix first.

faqs.q: Is every citation also a source, but not every source a citation?
faqs.a: Yes, that's the right way to think about it. A citation is a source that got formally credited by name for a specific claim. A source that influenced the answer without that formal credit is closer to a mention, or sometimes invisible entirely.

faqs.q: Do AI engines read more sources than they actually show in the final answer?
faqs.a: Generally yes. Different engines read varying numbers of candidate pages per answer and only surface a handful as visible citations, so most sources an engine reads never become visible to the person asking.

faqs.q: Does my page need backlinks to be treated as a trustworthy source?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Backlinks matter more for classic search ranking. For AI sourcing, clarity, structure and freshness tend to matter more directly than link-building history.

faqs.q: Can a page be a good source for one question and a bad one for a related question?
faqs.a: Yes. Being a source is decided per question, based on how directly the page answers that specific thing being asked, not as a fixed overall quality score.

faqs.q: Is structured data required for a page to be used as a source?
faqs.a: No, it's not required, but it reduces ambiguity for the model, since it doesn't have to infer a fact from prose when it's already given as explicit, machine-readable data.

faqs.q: What's the fastest way to check if my page even qualifies as a candidate source?
faqs.a: Run the free LLM Access Check at /check. If the real content isn't visible to the AI crawlers it tests, the page can't become a source no matter how strong the writing is.
